articles.title: Make API Usage Reports Useful to the Person Paying
articles.excerpt: A usage report should help an account owner understand what consumed the allowance or balance. A large total without unit or scope leaves that decision unresolved. Quick answer: Show the billable unit…
articles.body: A usage report should help an account owner understand what consumed the allowance or balance. A large total without unit or scope leaves that decision unresolved. Quick answer: Show the billable unit, reporting window, product scope and relevant breakdowns, with a path to appropriately restricted request evidence. Distinguish estimated usage, provider-reported consumption and final billing. Explain missing or delayed data and preserve retries where they affect interpretation. Start with the billing question For an illustrative extraction account, the owner may need to know whether a rise came from a larger batch, repeated attempts or a different operation. A dashboard showing only “requests” may not explain the actual billable unit.

articles.body: Đội nội dung thường hỏi đội kỹ thuật một câu: "Có cách nào kiểm tra nhanh từ khóa trong bài có đặt đúng chỗ không, mà không phải cài thêm plugin?". Bài này dựng một script Python nhỏ làm đúng việc đó: đo mật độ từ khóa và kiểm tra từ khóa có mặt ở các vị trí quan trọng của một file HTML. Trọng tâm không chỉ là code, mà là lý do thiết kế: vì sao script ưu tiên kiểm tra vị trí hơn đếm số lần. Bài toán: đo cái gì Mật độ từ khóa (keyword density) là tỷ lệ số lần từ khóa xuất hiện so với tổng số chữ của bài. Bài 1.000 chữ có từ khóa xuất hiện 10 lần thì mật độ là 1%. Đây là thứ dễ tính nhất, nhưng không phải thứ quan trọng nhất. Google không có con số mật độ chuẩn.

articles.body: Today on Decoder , I’m joined by Joey Brookhart, an analyst at the chip and AI research firm SemiAnalysis, to help me dig into the story inside the numbers of the Anthropic IPO filing — a document known as an S-1. Anthropic just filed its S-1 to go public on the Nasdaq, and it could start trading as soon as next month at a valuation of anywhere between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion. That would immediately make it one of the most valuable companies on the planet. But the price tag really isn’t the whole story here. The S-1 document published earlier this week is hundreds upon hundreds of pages filled with details that finally paint a picture of the economics of a frontier AI lab.

articles.title: We urgently need to monitor AI agents’ actions in real time
articles.excerpt: This summer, hundreds of OpenAI agents tried to cheat on a cybersecurity test. They broke out of their test environment and successfully hacked Hugging Face, a site that they believed held clues about…
articles.body: This summer, hundreds of OpenAI agents tried to cheat on a cybersecurity test. They broke out of their test environment and successfully hacked Hugging Face, a site that they believed held clues about how they’d be graded. Around the same time, another OpenAI agent accessed private files from an Australian government website. It’s a problem that’s by no means confined to OpenAI. In the months since, Anthropic, Google, and Meta have also disclosed incidents in which their agents have gone off track. And worryingly, in many cases the agents eluded the very researchers and safety teams tasked with monitoring them.  AI agents are taking unauthorized actions, and the companies building and running them are mostly relying on luck and hindsight to mitigate any harmful impacts.
